severity_taxonomy.CRITICAL: An active, exploitable boundary bypass or a mission invariant violated in a way that gives an attacker material capability today.
severity_taxonomy.HIGH: A control is absent or disabled such that a known attack path is open, protected currently only by accident, convention, or a detection gap.
severity_taxonomy.MEDIUM: A real defect with a bounded or conditional impact: fails closed, needs contention to trigger, or is confined to a non-tenant-facing path.
severity_taxonomy.LOW: A hardening gap, availability defect, or stale artifact with no credible path to tenant-boundary compromise.
severity_taxonomy.INFO: A coverage gap, accepted demo convention, or observation with no finding attached.

findings.title: Gateway control-plane namespace (ingress) carries zero NetworkPolicy
findings.detail: The ingress namespace, which hosts the Envoy Gateway control plane, has no NetworkPolicy. Its metrics port 19001 is reachable from any unprivileged tenant pod with no authentication.

findings.title: backend namespace carries zero NetworkPolicy
findings.detail: frontend can reach backend's MinIO, NATS, and Postgres with no policy on either side.

findings.title: frontend namespace carries zero NetworkPolicy
findings.detail: No blanket default-deny exists for the frontend namespace's three pods.

findings.title: fe-k8s-afm namespace carries zero NetworkPolicy
findings.detail: Single-pod namespace with no isolation. Smaller blast radius than NET-2/NET-3.

findings.title: cpai namespace carries zero NetworkPolicy
findings.detail: Single-pod namespace with no isolation.

findings.title: kagent namespace is only partially covered
findings.detail: kagent-postgres-isolation correctly scopes the controller-to-postgres path. kagent-controller, kagent-ui, and kagent-tools-metrics have no Ingress policy at all and no egress restriction.

findings.title: Platform namespaces carry zero NetworkPolicy
findings.detail: cert-manager, kube-system, spire-system, local-path-storage, and registry have no policy. A blanket default-deny risks breaking core cluster plumbing without a carefully scoped allowlist. Recorded as a lower-urgency follow-up, separate from the P2-1 tenant fixes.

findings.title: No ClientTrafficPolicy declares the XFF trust boundary
findings.detail: A client-supplied X-Forwarded-For entry remains present in the header chain. Envoy's current default is safe, but the trust boundary is implicit, not declared.

findings.title: HTTP/2 pseudo-header manipulation was not exhaustively tested
findings.detail: curl cannot forge invalid HTTP/2 framing independent of its own library. Recorded as a coverage gap (GW-H2-1), not asserted clean.

findings.title: No rate limiting middleware is installed anywhere in the application
findings.detail: No per-route or global rate limiting exists on fe-signalloom-api. All routes accept unbounded request volume from an authenticated or unauthenticated caller.

findings.title: Settings.cors_allowed_origins is declared but never wired to CORSMiddleware
findings.detail: The setting exists but has no effect. Browsers currently enforce the default same-origin policy, so the gap fails closed today, but the configuration is dead and misleading.

findings.title: CEL policy routes have no auth dependency
findings.detail: routers.policies's own CEL-validate, evaluate, and bundle routes carry no auth dependency. They are currently unreachable only by router-registration-order accident, not by a deliberate control.

findings.title: Ad-hoc error messages occasionally include raw exception text
findings.detail: Several routers return raw exception text to the caller instead of a sanitized error.

findings.title: threading.Lock held across an await in the enrollment fallback path
findings.detail: enroll_host_handler's in-memory fallback path holds a threading.Lock across an await point, a latent deadlock and availability risk under concurrent enrollment.

findings.title: Duplicate router registration breaks route-inventory invariant tests
findings.detail: Pre-existing defect, confirmed not caused by this card by removing its four new files from disk and reproducing identically. Inflates route counts and breaks several pre-existing inventory-exactness tests.

findings.title: Two OpenBao JWT roles issue 32-day tokens instead of the mission's 5-minute cap
findings.detail: signalloom-cardvault-agent and signalloom-fe-signalloom roles issue 768h (32-day) tokens. The mission's Fail-Closed Boundaries invariant requires a 5-minute hard cap on workload credentials.

findings.title: signalloom-agent-generic role's bound_claims glob is non-functional
findings.detail: Missing bound_claims_type=glob permanently denies all 18 registered fleet agents. Fails closed: an availability and correctness defect, not an active privilege-escalation bypass.

findings.title: Two of four live tenant identities have no corresponding OpenBao JWT role
findings.detail: A delegation gap, not a privilege-escalation path. Two SPIRE-registered agent-trust tenant identities cannot authenticate to OpenBao at all.

findings.title: SPIRE agent runs with insecure_bootstrap and skip_kubelet_verification enabled
findings.detail: Demo-appropriate today. Flag explicitly before any path toward a production deployment.

findings.title: agent-cardvault's Workload API socket is mounted via raw hostPath
findings.detail: The documented spiffe-csi-driver ephemeral volume is not used for this one agent.

findings.title: A static root token is hardcoded across multiple live ConfigMaps and Jobs
findings.detail: Accepted pre-existing demo convention (signalloom-demo-root-token).

findings.title: The live sentinel's eBPF telemetry has zero process, ptrace, or namespace visibility
findings.detail: The deployed eBPF program attaches only tp_btf/inet_sock_set_state (TCP flow state). A fuller syscall tracer exists in-repo but is wired into no cmd/ entrypoint and is not deployed. Evading telemetry via process spawning, ptrace, or unshare succeeds trivially today because there is no instrumentation to evade. A detection-scope gap, not a bypass of a working defense.

findings.title: cgroup-freeze intermittently exceeds the daemon's internal deadline under host contention
findings.detail: Freezing a cgroup containing a process that has unshare(CLONE_NEWPID)'d with mount_proc returned HTTP 504 in 2 of 5 runs against the isolated test instance under shared-node contention. Once the freeze call completes it is unconditionally effective. Not a containment bypass: a latency and reliability finding against one workload shape under load.

findings.title: A sibling test harness is stale against the current binary's auth contract
findings.detail: scripts/test-cgroup-freezer.sh (owned by CRKC-P1-2) sets only STUN_RESUME_TOKEN and sends no Authorization header, while the binary now requires STUN_FREEZE_TOKEN and bearer-gates /stun. Outside this card's merge boundary.
